report:
Feature 1 (Accounts) is written and committed as `e7dcbac` on the current branch, not pushed. `yarn architecture gate --base ccf7f75… --mode architecture --fix` passes all of its checks: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked done.

**What the API does**
- **`POST /v1/accounts`** answers `202 { operationId }`. The outcome is read at `GET /v1/operations/{id}`, with the new account's id as its `result`. A refused value ends as `ERROR` with the rule's name: `InvalidEmailFormat`, `PasswordTooShort`, `NoRole`, `UnknownRole` or `EmailAlreadyUsed` (an email already used is refused whatever its case). A body missing a field or with a field of the wrong type gets `400`.
- **`POST /v1/accounts/login`** answers `200 { token }` at once. A wrong password and an unknown email get the same `401`.
- **`GET /v1/accounts/me`** answers `200 { id, email, roles }`, or `401` with no token or a token that proves nothing.
- **Persistence:** I ran a real server on port 19270, signed up, killed it with `kill -9` and started it again on the same file. The account was still there, and the token issued before the kill still worked.

**Architecture work (ADR 2, `docs/adr/0002-one-sqlite-file-and-its-unit-of-work.md`)**
- **SQLite storage:** I used Node's built-in `node:sqlite`, so there is no new dependency. A SQLite unit of work stores a transaction's writes and its outbox entries together at commit, or nothing on rollback. Events that a crash left unpublished are published when the server starts again.
- **One change under `src/Architecture`:** `UnitOfWork` gains an optional `run()`. The execution context calls it around each transaction's work, which lets the SQLite adapters join the current transaction without the ports or handlers naming it.
- **Transport changes:**
  - The unit of work is now passed in from the composition root.
  - Fastify no longer coerces body types, because by default it would turn a wrong type into the right one instead of answering `400`.
  - Operations are served at `/v1/operations/:id` as well as `/v1/tracker/operations/:id`.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Sign-in:** the storm says signing in is not a fact of the domain, so I made it an `Authentication` service exported from the Accounts wiring file rather than a command or a query. Adding a query would have made the code's inventory differ from the storm's.
- **Async sign-up:** the project's checklist says a command answers `202`, so sign-up does that. The product brief would also have allowed answering `201 { id }` at once.
- **Email format:** I reused the shared kernel's `Email`, which requires at least two characters after the last dot, so `a@b.c` is refused. That is slightly stricter than the product's wording ("something with a dot"), and I didn't change the shared kernel.
- **Two simultaneous sign-ups with the same email:** both can pass the uniqueness check. The database's unique index stops the second one, but that sign-up ends as an `ERROR` named `Unknown` rather than `EmailAlreadyUsed`.
- **Operation records stay in memory:** after a restart, `/v1/operations/{id}` no longer knows an earlier operation. Accounts survive; the status of a sign-up made before the restart does not.
- **Tokens:** they are HMAC-signed and last 7 days. The secret is `TOKEN_SECRET` when it is set; otherwise one is generated once and stored in the database file.
- **Roles:** "traveller" and "host" are kept inside the Accounts context. A signed-in caller is the shared kernel's `Role.USER`, so the existing sign-in check works unchanged.

Feature 2, publish a listing, is built and committed as `fc33ecb` on the current branch (not pushed). The gate (`--base e7dcbac --mode architecture --fix`) passes on all its checks: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and e2e tests. The storm owes nothing; the gate marked it `done`.

**What the API now does**
- **Every route** in the table is served under `/v1/listings`. Commands answer `202 { operationId }`, and the draft's operation result is `{ id }`.
- **Creating:** only a signed-in host can draft. An account without the host role is refused with `NotAHost`.
- **Values:** a value outside the rules is refused by the domain with a named error (`InvalidTitle`, `InvalidCity`, `InvalidCapacity`, `NightlyPriceTooLow`, `InvalidCleaningFee`, `UnknownCancellationPolicy`). Only a body of the wrong shape gets a 400.
- **Changes:** only the listing's host changes it (`NotTheListingHost`). The host can replace the description until it is archived.
- **Its life:** publish works from draft or suspended, suspend only from published, and archive from any state. After archiving, everything is refused (`ListingIsArchived`). Publishing again records `ListingPublished` again and keeps the first publication time, as the storm decided.
- **Who sees it:** `GET /listings/{id}` shows a published listing to anyone; any other state answers 404 to everyone except its host. `GET /listings/mine` lists the host's own listings, newest first.
- **Storage:** listings are kept in the same SQLite file as accounts.

**The link to Accounts:** Listings asks whether an account is a host through its own port (`Hosts`), answered from Accounts' existing account read model. Accounts' wiring now exports that read model so Listings' wiring can use it. The decision is written up in `docs/adr/0003-listings-asks-accounts-who-is-a-host.md`, and the Accounts → Listings relationship in `conventions/domain.yaml` is no longer marked `planned`.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **"The API works as request 1 says":** I read it as working like feature 1 — the operation is followed at `/v1/operations/{id}`, and its result is `{ id }` because the table says so (sign-up returns a bare id string).
- **Refusals the brief didn't list:** publishing an already published listing (`CannotPublish`) and archiving an archived one (`ListingIsArchived`).
- **Strangers acting on a hidden listing:** if someone else sends a command to a draft, they get `NotTheListingHost`, not "not found". So a person who already has the id can tell it exists, though they cannot read it. Hiding it completely would mean checking visibility in each handler.
- **Losing the host role:** only drafting asks Accounts. An account that loses the role can still change the listings it already has.
- **Whole numbers:** capacity and both prices must be whole numbers (cents). The domain enforces this; the request schema only checks they are numbers.
- **Accounts' read model:** it is the account owner's view, which happens to include the roles. If Accounts later offers a view meant for other contexts, the adapter should move to it.

Search works and is committed on the current branch as `6d8289a` (not pushed). The gate (`--base fc33ecb… --mode architecture --fix`) passes on every step: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and e2e tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked done.

**What it does**
- **Route:** Booking answers `GET /v1/listings?city=&checkIn=&checkOut=&guests=`. Its route sits under `/listings` next to Listings' own routes.
- **Refusals:** a search that makes no sense gets `400` with a named reason: `MissingCity`, `IncompleteStay`, `InvalidDate`, `EmptyStay` or `InvalidGuests`. Booking's domain decides these (`SearchCriteria`, `Stay`).
- **Finding listings:** Booking asks Listings through a port it owns, `IListingTerms` (ListingTerms in the storm). The port's documentation states the order: lowest nightly price, then first published, then id. Listings sorts in SQL and the search handler never re-sorts.
- **Matching:** the city matches whatever its case. Only published listings that take the number of guests are found. With dates, Booking also drops listings that can't give every night of the stay (`ICalendars`, kept in a `calendar_nights` table).
- **Architecture:** the Listings → Booking relationship is no longer `planned` in `conventions/domain.yaml`. The decision is in `docs/adr/0004-booking-asks-listings-for-terms.md`.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Where the order's contract test lives.** The storm says the order is held "on the port, in its contract test". But the linter forbids Booking's tests from importing Listings' Infrastructure. So the real test of the order is in Listings' `SqliteListingQueries.spec.ts`. Booking's adapter test only checks that the order is passed on unchanged.
- **Two ports in one query handler.** The query checklist says a handler reads one port. The storm's decision (ask Listings, then keep what the calendar allows) needs two. I followed the storm: `IListingTerms` is the handler's port and `ICalendars` is passed in its constructor.
- **No calendar data yet.** No feature writes nights yet, so every night counts as free. I made the table now rather than a stand-in, so the blocked-nights and booking features only have to write to it.
- **Reading `guests`.** The app never converts query-string text to numbers, so the schema declares `guests` as text. The controller turns it into a number, and the domain refuses anything that isn't a whole number of at least 1. So `guests=many` gets `400 InvalidGuests`, and an empty `guests=` counts as not given (1 guest).
- **Error body.** A refused search also returns the reason's `type` alongside `message`, so the client can act on it. The spec only says `400`.
- **Case matching is plain-alphabet only.** It uses SQLite's case-insensitive comparison, so accented capitals only match when written the same way.
- **Invalid dates.** Something that isn't a real date (e.g. `2026-02-30`) is refused as `InvalidDate`. The spec doesn't name this case.

head: 6d8289a7040d47fbf792984f8b4d9797fbe271f7
report: /runs/openstay/clean-w/app.flow/worktrees/pilot-clean-w/grade-search-1793532246106.json

Feature 4 (the host's calendar) is built and committed as `97948af` on the current branch, not pushed. `yarn architecture gate --base 6d8289a… --mode architecture --fix` passes on every check: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and the gate marked it done.

**No architecture task was needed.** Booking already existed, and so did the Listings → Booking link through `ListingTerms` (ADR 4). So I added no context, relationship or ADR. I only gave the existing `ListingTerms` port one more method, `of(listingId)`, and two more fields, `minNights` and `maxNights`.

**What was built:**
- **Stay limits (Listings).** A listing takes 1 to 365 nights until its host sets other limits. `PUT /v1/listings/{id}/stay-limits` sets them. It refuses limits outside 1–365 or not whole numbers (`InvalidStayLimits`), a shortest above the longest (`MinNightsAboveMaxNights`), and anyone but the host. `GET /v1/listings/{id}` now shows `minNights` and `maxNights`.
- **Blocking and freeing nights (Booking).** There is one `ListingCalendar` per listing. `POST /v1/listings/{id}/block` and `/unblock` take `{ from, to }`. Only the host can use them; Booking learns who the host is from the listing's terms. A range is 1 to 365 nights, and a bad one is refused as `InvalidDate`, `EmptyRange` or `RangeTooLong`. Blocking a night that is already blocked, or freeing one that is not, succeeds and changes nothing.
- **The calendar.** `GET /v1/listings/{id}/calendar?from=&to=` answers `[{ date, available }]` in date order. Anyone sees it for a published listing; for a draft, suspended or archived one, only its host does, and everyone else gets 404, as with the listing page.
- **Search.** It now leaves out a listing when a night of the stay is blocked, or when the stay is shorter or longer than the listing takes.

**Choices I made where the brief was unclear:**
1. **Blocking a booked night.** No bookings exist yet, so the calendar only holds blocked nights and nothing refuses a block. Each stored night now has a reason column (`blocked` for now), so the later request can add its own nights and the refusal next to them.
2. **Creating a calendar records no event.** A calendar is created the first time its host blocks or frees nights. CLAUDE.md says a creation records an event, but the storm lists only `NightsBlocked` and `NightsUnblocked`, so I followed the storm.
3. **No event when nothing changes.** A block or unblock that changes nothing records no event. The events carry only the nights that actually changed.
4. **The calendar read has the same 1–365-night limit as a block.** A wrong range answers 400 with the rule's name. The brief didn't say what to do with a bad range on this read.
5. **Changing the limits.** Only the host can change them, and not once the listing is archived. Search keeps to them; nothing else uses them yet.
6. **Existing database files.** The new columns `listings.min_nights`, `listings.max_nights` and `calendar_nights.reason` are added automatically to an older database file.

New specs cover the calendar, the stay limits, the block and unblock handlers, the storage, and an end-to-end case for the whole API. Two existing tests that compare a listing exactly now expect `minNights` and `maxNights`.

head: 97948af62c3ba76da50b85588b39f6e40c294381

The quote feature is built and committed on the current branch as `c252c04` (not pushed). `yarn architecture gate --base 97948af… --mode architecture --fix` passes: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and e2e tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**Architecture task:** the feature needed one new link between contexts, Accounts → Booking through a port Booking owns (`Travellers`). The context map already listed it as `planned`; I removed `planned` in `conventions/domain.yaml` and recorded the decision in `docs/adr/0005-a-quote-is-its-own-aggregate.md`, which is also linked from the ADR index.

**Listings, the tourist tax:**
- The host declares it with `PUT /v1/listings/{id}/tourist-tax`. It is whole cents, 0 or more, and 0 until declared.
- Declaring it records `TouristTaxDeclared`. A bad amount is refused with `InvalidTouristTax` behind the 202; a body of the wrong shape gets a 400.
- `GET /v1/listings/{id}` now shows `touristTax`, and Booking reads it through `ListingTerms`.
- Older database files get the new column with a default of 0.

**Booking, the quote:**
- `Quote` is its own aggregate, as the storm decided. `Quote.give()` makes each refusal a named failure: `ListingNotPublished`, `TooManyGuests`, `CheckInInThePast`, `NightsNotAvailable`, `StayLengthNotTaken`, `OwnListing`. An account without the traveller role gets `NotATraveller`.
- A quote copies the lines and the cancellation policy when it is given and is never changed, so later changes to the listing don't touch it. The e2e test checks this.
- It records `StayQuoted`.
- The lines are always these four, in cents: Nights (`host`), Cleaning fee (`host`), Tourist tax (`external`, guests × nights × tax), and Platform fee (`platform`, 0). The total is their sum.
- `GET /v1/quotes/{id}` answers 200 only to the traveller who asked, 404 to anyone else, and 401 without a sign-in.

**One change outside the feature:** the inventory tool reads only one route mount per context, and the last one registered wins. Mounting quotes at `/quotes` made the tool report the existing search and calendar routes under `/quotes/...`. To fix it without touching the tool, I now mount all Booking routes at `/` and wrote the full path in each route file. The public API is unchanged and the existing e2e tests still pass.

**What was unclear, and what I decided:**
- **Where `QUOTE_TTL_SECONDS` is read:** the hot spot says "the composition root", but each context's module is built at import time. I read it in Booking's `module.local.ts`, as `DATABASE_PATH` already is, and pass it to the handler. A value that is missing or not a positive number falls back to 1800.
- **Line labels:** the product didn't name them, so I chose "Nights", "Cleaning fee", "Tourist tax" and "Platform fee". If other language servers have to match exactly, these are the strings to align.
- **Listings that don't exist:** a quote for one gets 404 (`NotFoundException`). One that exists but isn't published is refused with `ListingNotPublished`.
- **"Before today":** today is the UTC date. A check-in today is accepted.
- **Expired quotes:** they can still be read. Whether one can still be booked is left to the booking feature.
- **Nights not held:** a quote doesn't reserve its nights, so two travellers can hold quotes for the same nights.

head: c252c04bf0d0140e47092d5f739a940b131844ee
report: /runs/openstay/clean-w/app.flow/worktrees/pilot-clean-w/grade-quote-1793533377085.json

Feature 6 (book instantly) is built and committed on the current branch as `d13936f`; nothing was pushed. The gate (`--base c252c04… --mode architecture --fix`) passes and marked the storm done, and the storm now owes nothing. One gap: if two servers book the same night at once, the loser is refused, but not by the usual name (details below).

**What was built**
- **A booking is its own aggregate.** `Booking.confirm()` refuses a quote that has expired (`QuoteExpired`) and a listing that is no longer published (`ListingNotPublished`). It copies the quote's lines, total and cancellation policy, and records `BookingConfirmed`.
- **The calendar takes the nights.** `ListingCalendar.take()` refuses any night that is blocked or already taken (`NightsNotAvailable`) and records `NightsTaken`. The host can no longer block a booked night (`NightsBooked`).
- **Both are saved in one transaction.** A small domain service, `StayBooking`, decides the booking; the handler saves the calendar and the booking together. When two travellers race, the calendar's version refuses the second, the base handler tries again on fresh data, and the second is refused as `NightsNotAvailable`. The e2e test sends four simultaneous bookings for the same nights: exactly one is confirmed and the other three get that refusal.
- **Booked nights are taken everywhere.** A booked night is a row in `calendar_nights` with reason `booked` and the booking's id. The listing and the night form the primary key, so the database itself never holds a night twice. Search, the calendar and quotes already read every row, so they needed no change.
- **`Idempotency-Key`** is stored with the booking and unique per traveller. Sending a key the same traveller already used answers that booking's id and records nothing.
- **Reading bookings:**
  - `GET /bookings/{id}` is for the traveller and the listing's host; anyone else gets 404.
  - `GET /bookings/mine` lists the traveller's bookings.
  - `GET /listings/{id}/bookings` is for the listing's host only.
  - Both lists put the most recently made booking first.
- **Records:** ADR 6 (`docs/adr/0006-a-booking-takes-its-nights-from-the-calendar.md`), linked from the ADR index. I added a unit spec (`Booking.spec.ts`) and an e2e spec (`booking.routes.e2e.spec.ts`). `idempotency-key` is added to the CORS allowed headers.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Booking someone else's quote** is refused with `NotFound`, the same answer `GET /quotes/{id}` gives anyone but its traveller. The spec only says "refused", so this could instead be a named rule.
- **`POST /bookings`** answers `202 { operationId }`, and the booking's `{ id }` is the operation's result, as every other command here does. The spec's "creates the booking, `{ id }`" could be read as a direct answer.
- **A night taken since the quote** reuses `NightsNotAvailable`, the name a quote already gives that rule, rather than a new exception.
- **Two servers racing on one database file:** the second commit still fails, so exactly one booking is confirmed. But that failure surfaces as an unexpected error, not a conflict the handler retries, so the loser isn't refused as `NightsNotAvailable`. Fixing that belongs in `src/Architecture`, which a feature may not touch. ADR 6 records it as a consequence. Only the single-server race is tested.
- **The same key sent at the same instant:** the second request loses on the calendar's version, is retried, finds the key and answers the first booking. This case is not covered by a test.
- **An expired quote** is tested in the unit spec, using a clock parameter, but not end to end.

head: d13936f120cc08bb57b6a34c9b1818486609d5be
report: /runs/openstay/clean-w/app.flow/worktrees/pilot-clean-w/grade-book-instantly-1793533936851.json

Request-to-book is built and committed on the current branch as `e15147b` (not pushed). `yarn architecture gate --base d13936f… --mode architecture --fix` passes on every step: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, 172 unit tests and 63 e2e tests. The storm owes nothing and the gate marked it done. No new context or relationship was needed, because the booking mode reaches Booking through the existing ListingTerms port (ADR 4). The design is recorded in `docs/adr/0007-a-request-holds-its-nights-until-it-is-decided-or-expires.md`.

**What changed**
- **Listings:** `PUT /v1/listings/{id}/booking-mode` sets `instant` or `request`. Any other value is refused as `UnknownBookingMode` behind the 202, not as a 400. `GET /v1/listings/{id}` now shows `bookingMode`, and listings are `instant` until their host changes it.
- **Booking:** at a listing in `request` mode, `POST /v1/bookings` makes a booking with status `requested` and an `expiresAt`. `POST /v1/bookings/{id}/accept` confirms it and `POST /v1/bookings/{id}/decline` declines it and frees its nights. Only the listing's host decides, and only while the request is waiting.
- **Expiry without anyone acting:** while a request waits, the calendar holds its nights only until `expiresAt`. Once that passes, the nights are free straight away for booking, quoting, blocking and search. `GET /v1/bookings/{id}` reads it as `expired` before anything is written.
- **The sweep:** every `BOOKING_REQUEST_SWEEP_SECONDS` (60 by default), the app records each overdue request as expired and releases its nights, one transaction each.
- **Tests:** new unit tests and a new e2e spec, `booking-request.routes.e2e.spec.ts`, which uses a 3-second time limit to cover expiry.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **How the sweep runs.** There was no scheduler, so I added `FastifyApplication.every()` in Bootstrap. The sweep sends an internal `ExpireBookingRequest` command that no route builds and that refuses any signed-in caller. The storm doesn't name this command, but the storm check allows it. The inventory lists its caller as "anyone", which is not true in practice because nothing outside the app can reach it.
- **The sweep interval** is my own addition (`BOOKING_REQUEST_SWEEP_SECONDS`). The feature only specified `BOOKING_REQUEST_TTL_SECONDS`.
- **The storm lists BookStay's events as `[BookingRequested, NightsTaken]`.** I kept `BookingConfirmed` for instant bookings; the check only asks that the storm's events be among the ones recorded.
- **Accepting a request records no calendar event.** The calendar just makes the held nights permanent, because the storm gives accept only `BookingRequestAccepted`.
- **Who sees which error:** a traveller who tries to accept their own request gets `NotTheBookingHost`. Anyone who is neither the traveller nor the host gets `NotFound`, the same as when they try to read the booking.
- **Notifications:** the storm hints that the host will be told of new bookings and requests, but its `links` list is empty. I left Notifications untouched; the link to it stays marked `planned`.

head: e15147bb00b928120ba8f85e5279733e1743eba7
report: /runs/openstay/clean-w/app.flow/worktrees/pilot-clean-w/grade-request-to-book-1793534597771.json

Feature 8 (cancel a booking) is built and committed on the current branch as `c8acb56`; nothing was pushed. The gate (`yarn architecture gate --base e15147b… --mode architecture --fix`) passes on every check, including unit and e2e tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**No architecture task was needed.** The feature stays inside the Booking context, so I added no new context, relationship or ADR.

**What it does:**
- **Cancelling:** `POST /v1/bookings/{id}/cancel` answers 202. The traveller who booked or the listing's host can cancel a confirmed booking, once, and its nights are freed in the same transaction. Anyone else gets `NotFound`, as when reading the booking. Cancelling a booking that isn't confirmed, including a second time, is refused as `BookingNotConfirmed`.
- **What is refundable:** the booking works it out from the policy it was made under, its lines, who cancels and today's date.
  - The tourist tax is always refundable.
  - If the host cancels, everything is refundable.
  - If the traveller cancels, the host's lines follow the policy table by days before check-in, counted in UTC. A half is rounded down to the cent.
- **Reading it back:** `GET /v1/bookings/{id}` now shows `status: cancelled`, `cancellation: { by, at, refundable }` and `refund: { amount, status: "owed" }`. Nothing ever sets `refunded`; that is left for payments.
- **Storage:** the bookings table gets four new columns, added automatically to a database file created before this feature.

**Tests:** the domain tests cover every row of the policy table, the rounding and the edge days. A new e2e file, `cancel-booking.routes.e2e.spec.ts`, covers both kinds of cancellation over the API. It also checks that a booking keeps its policy after the host changes the listing's, and that the freed nights can be quoted again.

**Decisions I made where the brief was unclear:**
- **Platform fee line:** "the rest of the total (the host's lines)" doesn't say what happens to it. I count it with the host's lines, so the policy share applies to it too. It is 0 today, so no amount changes.
- **Cancelling after check-in:** the brief only covers the day of check-in. A negative day count is treated like the day itself, so the traveller gets back only the tourist tax.
- **Host who is also the traveller:** if someone books their own listing, a cancellation counts as by the traveller, which is the less generous rule.
- **Refused requests:** they come back as named errors on the operation (`NotABookingParty`, `BookingNotConfirmed`), following the API rule that a refusal is the operation's error behind the 202.
- **Unknown stored policy:** a policy that isn't `flexible`, `moderate` or `strict` makes the refund calculation throw, because it can only mean corrupted data.

head: c8acb568586226e3d72404dd913bb82a4b78eb66
report: /runs/openstay/clean-w/app.flow/worktrees/pilot-clean-w/grade-cancel-a-booking-1793535016655.json

The booking history and the contact rule are in, committed on the current branch as `4a7e6c0` (not pushed). `yarn architecture gate --base c8acb56… --mode architecture --fix` passes, including unit and e2e tests, and the storm now owes nothing; the gate marked it `done`.

**What was built**
- **History:** each change to a booking's state is now recorded with who made it and when, in the order it happened:
  - a request: by its traveller;
  - a booking confirmed at once: by nobody;
  - an accepted or declined request: by the host;
  - a cancellation: by whoever cancelled;
  - an expired request: by nobody, at its expiry time.

  These entries go into a new `booking_history` table in the same database transaction as the booking's state, so the two can't disagree. The booking itself doesn't keep or use the history.
- **`GET /v1/bookings/{id}/history`:** the traveller and the host can read it, oldest first. Anyone else gets 404, and a caller who isn't signed in gets 401.
- **Contact:** `GET /v1/bookings/{id}` now includes `contact: { email }`, the other party's, when the booking is confirmed or cancelled; otherwise `contact` is `null`. The email is read from Accounts at that moment through a new port Booking owns (`IContactDetails`, answered by `AccountsContactDetails`), and Booking stores no copy.
- **Architecture records:** the link from Accounts to Booking already existed, so no new relationship was needed. I added ADR 8 and its line in the ADR index, and pointed that link's description in `conventions/domain.yaml` at it.
- **Tests:** new tests cover how a booking records its changes, history for older bookings, and an end-to-end run of the history and contact rules. One existing e2e expectation in `booking.routes.e2e.spec.ts` now includes `contact`.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
1. **Bookings made before this feature:** "a history from the state they were in" could mean one entry or a reconstructed sequence. I give one entry, the current state. When the record says who made it (traveller, host or canceller) that person is named, otherwise nobody. The time is the cancellation or expiry time if stored, otherwise the booking time. So a request that was accepted before this feature shows as "confirmed by the host" at the time it was booked; ADR 8 says so.
2. **A request past its deadline:** if the background job hasn't marked it expired yet, the history still ends with `expired`, by nobody, at the deadline. That matches how the booking itself already reads.
3. **Contact on a cancelled booking:** a booking can only be cancelled after it was confirmed, so "cancelled" alone is enough to show the email.
4. **How the history is written:** I kept it in the repository's save rather than having a separate listener build it from published events. A listener would run in its own transaction and could receive the same event twice, which a simple ordered history doesn't need.
